q: Fluid is a substance that offers no ____ resistance to deforming forces.
e: Fluid is a substance that offers no permanent resistance to deforming forces. A fluid has no permanent resistance to a deforming force.

q: Fluid statics concentrates on fluids at rest, while fluid dynamics concerns with the fluid in ____.
e: Fluid statics concentrates on fluids at rest, while fluid dynamics concerns with the fluid in motion. Fluid dynamics studies fluids in motion; statics studies fluids at rest.

q: Motion of fluids is an important application in our daily life; such as river flow, water distribution systems, gas pipelines, ____ (travels in air) and motion underneath the surface of water.
e: The blank is aviation. That word is the one that completes the idea about Motion fluids important application daily life.

q: The study of the flow of liquid is called hydrodynamics, whereas hydrostatic is the study of liquid at ____.
e: The study of the flow of liquid is called hydrodynamics, whereas hydrostatic is the study of liquid at rest. Fluid statics is about fluids at rest.

q: Fluid is either liquid or ____.
e: Fluid is either liquid or gas. A gas has no fixed volume; p, V and T follow Boyle and Charles.

q: The volume of a gas depends on pressure and temperature obeying Boyle's law and ____ law.
e: The volume of a gas depends on pressure and temperature obeying Boyle's law and Charles' law. Charles' law links gas volume to temperature at constant pressure.

q: However, the volume of a liquid does not depend on ____ if the temperature is constant.
e: However, the volume of a liquid does not depend on pressure if the temperature is constant. Along a streamline a speed rise is paid for by a pressure drop.

q: Hence, the liquid is incompressible (i.e. density of liquid is ____ for any pressure provided that the temperature is kept constant).
e: Hence, the liquid is incompressible (i.e. density of liquid is constant for any pressure provided that the temperature is kept constant). constant is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: In the flow of fluids, the path or flow of the fluid particles is called ____.
e: In the flow of fluids, the path or flow of the fluid particles is called streamline. A streamline is the path a fluid particle follows. In steady laminar flow, streamlines do not cross.

q: Motion of fluids can be classified by two types, laminar flow and ____ flow.
e: Motion of fluids can be classified by two types, laminar flow and turbulent flow. Turbulent flow is irregular and whirling, so speed and direction at a point keep changing.

q: If fluid particles are moving steady in smooth paths in layers, with each layer moving smoothly past the adjacent layers with no mixing; such a flow is called ____ flow.
e: If fluid particles are moving steady in smooth paths in layers, with each layer moving smoothly past the adjacent layers with no mixing; such a flow is called laminar flow. Laminar flow moves in smooth layers with no mixing between neighbouring sheets.

q: In this steady laminar flow, ____ do not cross each other and every fluid particle arriving at a given point has the same velocity.
e: In this steady laminar flow, streamlines do not cross each other and every fluid particle arriving at a given point has the same velocity. A streamline is the path a fluid particle follows. In steady laminar flow, streamlines do not cross.

q: If the flow or path of the fluid particles are irregular, their direction is always changing or whirling; this fluid movement is called ____ flow.
e: If the flow or path of the fluid particles are irregular, their direction is always changing or whirling; this fluid movement is called turbulent flow. Turbulent flow is irregular and whirling, so speed and direction at a point keep changing.

q: In turbulent flow the speed of the fluid at a point is continuously undergoing changes in both magnitude and ____.
e: In turbulent flow the speed of the fluid at a point is continuously undergoing changes in both magnitude and direction. On a circle the velocity direction keeps turning even if the speed is steady.

q: Ideal laminar fluid flow considers the following facts: The fluid is ____.
e: Ideal laminar fluid flow considers the following facts: The fluid is incompressible. Laminar flow moves in smooth layers with no mixing between neighbouring sheets.

q: The flow has no friction or friction is neglected (Internal friction in fluids is called ____ ; and hence, zero viscosity).
e: The flow has no friction or friction is neglected (Internal friction in fluids is called viscosity ; and hence, zero viscosity). Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: The fluid flow is laminar (steady) and ____ flow is not taken into account.
e: The fluid flow is laminar (steady) and turbulent flow is not taken into account. Turbulent flow is irregular and whirling, so speed and direction at a point keep changing.

q: For example, sea breeze is a laminar flow and storm is a ____ flow.
e: For example, sea breeze is a laminar flow and storm is a turbulent flow. Turbulent flow is irregular and whirling, so speed and direction at a point keep changing.

q: Consider an ideal fluid there must be laminar flow and no ____.
e: Consider an ideal fluid there must be laminar flow and no viscosity. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: The mass flowing in section 1 must equal the ____ flowing in section 2.
e: The mass flowing in section 1 must equal the mass flowing in section 2. Continuity of an incompressible fluid keeps mass flow the same at every section.

q: The equation (3.1) states that the liquid entering one end of the pipe leaves from the other end with a constant ____ flow rate.
e: The equation (3.1) states that the liquid entering one end of the pipe leaves from the other end with a constant volume flow rate. Volume flow rate Av is constant for an incompressible liquid in a pipe.

q: The larger the area of the pipe, the ____ is the speed; and the smaller the area, the faster is the speed.
e: The larger the area of the pipe, the slower is the speed; and the smaller the area, the faster is the speed. Continuity: a larger pipe area gives a slower flow speed.

q: For example, the speed of water spraying from a hose increases by making the hose area ____.
e: For example, the speed of water spraying from a hose increases by making the hose area smaller. A smaller nozzle area raises the exit speed because Av stays constant.

q: Bernoulli's equation, in fluid dynamics, relates the pressure, flow speed, and ____ for the steady (laminar) flow of an ideal incompressible fluid.
e: Bernoulli's equation, in fluid dynamics, relates the pressure, flow speed, and height for the steady (laminar) flow of an ideal incompressible fluid. Laminar flow moves in smooth layers with no mixing between neighbouring sheets.

q: The internal friction of the fluid flow is negligible (i.e. no ____).
e: The internal friction of the fluid flow is negligible (i.e. no viscosity). Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: Bernoulli's equation can be derived using the ____ principle to a fluid flowing in a tube.
e: Bernoulli's equation can be derived using the work-energy principle to a fluid flowing in a tube. Bernoulli's equation keeps p + ½ρv² + ρgh constant along a streamline for incompressible, non-viscous laminar flow.

q: According to work-energy principle, the work done on this section of fluid must equal the change in total ____ energy (i.e. kinetic energy+potential energy).
e: According to work-energy principle, the work done on this section of fluid must equal the change in total mechanical energy (i.e. kinetic energy+potential energy). mechanical is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The cross-sectional area, speed and ____ at two ends of the fluid section are $A_1$, $v_1$, $p_1$ and $A_2$, $v_2$, $p_2$, respectively.
e: The cross-sectional area, speed and pressure at two ends of the fluid section are A₁, v₁, p₁ and A₂, v₂, p₂, respectively. Along a streamline a speed rise is paid for by a pressure drop.

q: The work done on the fluid in this case is due to the ____ of the fluid.
e: The work done on the fluid in this case is due to the pressure of the fluid. Along a streamline a speed rise is paid for by a pressure drop.

q: In words, Bernoulli's theorem states that the sum of pressure energy, kinetic energy and potential energy per unit ____ of an incompressible, non-viscous fluid in a streamlined laminar flow remains constant.
e: The blank is volume. Volume flow rate Av is constant for an incompressible liquid in a pipe. That word is the one that completes the idea about words Bernoulli theorem states sum pressure.

q: The air flow moving above the top curved surface of the wing has a longer distance to travel and needs to go ____ to have the same transit time as the air travelling along the lower flat surface.
e: The blank is faster. That word is the one that completes the idea about air flow moving above top curved.

q: This causes a low pressure above the wing and a high pressure below the wing which provides a ____ on the wing.
e: This causes a low pressure above the wing and a high pressure below the wing which provides a lift on the wing. Faster air over a wing lowers pressure there and the difference is lift.

q: When the piston of the sprayer is pressed, the fast moving air causes a ____ pressure at the tip of the nozzle.
e: When the piston of the sprayer is pressed, the fast moving air causes a low pressure at the tip of the nozzle. Bernoulli: high speed goes with low pressure.

q: The liquid inside the container is at a ____ pressure, and therefore rushes up through the stem and out the nozzle.
e: The liquid inside the container is at a higher pressure, and therefore rushes up through the stem and out the nozzle. The still fluid sits at higher pressure than the fast stream.

q: The ____ effect is a particular manifestation of Bernoulli's theorem that is commonly associated with a spinning object moving through a fluid.
e: The Magnus effect is a particular manifestation of Bernoulli's theorem that is commonly associated with a spinning object moving through a fluid. Bernoulli's equation keeps p + ½ρv² + ρgh constant along a streamline for incompressible, non-viscous laminar flow.

q: In the case of a ball spinning through the air, the turning ball drags some of the ____ around with it.
e: In the case of a ball spinning through the air, the turning ball drags some of the air around with it. air is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The effect is named after the German physicist ____, who described the effect in 1852.
e: The effect is named after the German physicist Heinrich Gustav Magnus, who described the effect in 1852. Heinrich Gustav Magnus is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: During cyclones, moving air gain speed above the roof of a house causing the ____ pressure on the roof.
e: During cyclones, moving air gain speed above the roof of a house causing the reduced pressure on the roof. reduced is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Therefore the pressure inside the house is ____, which can raise the roof.
e: Therefore the pressure inside the house is greater, which can raise the roof. greater is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Most of the fluids are not ideal ones and offer some ____ to motion.
e: Most of the fluids are not ideal ones and offer some resistance to motion. resistance is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The resistance to fluid motion (or) internal resistance of fluid is called ____.
e: The resistance to fluid motion (or) internal resistance of fluid is called viscosity. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: Viscosity arises when there is ____ motion between layers of the fluid.
e: Viscosity arises when there is relative motion between layers of the fluid. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: More precisely, it measures resistance to flow arising due to the internal friction between the fluid layers as they ____ past one another when fluid flows.
e: More precisely, it measures resistance to flow arising due to the internal friction between the fluid layers as they slip past one another when fluid flows. slip is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Viscosity can also be thought of as a measure of a fluid's ____ (stickiness) or its resistance to objects passing through it.
e: Viscosity can also be thought of as a measure of a fluid's thickness (stickiness) or its resistance to objects passing through it. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: A fluid with large viscosity resists motion because its strong ____ forces give it a lot of internal friction.
e: A fluid with large viscosity resists motion because its strong intermolecular forces give it a lot of internal friction. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: A fluid with low viscosity flows easily because its molecular make up results in very little ____ when it is in motion.
e: A fluid with low viscosity flows easily because its molecular make up results in very little friction when it is in motion. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: The viscosity of liquids ____ rapidly with an increase in temperature, and the viscosity of gases increases with an increase in temperature.
e: The viscosity of liquids decreases rapidly with an increase in temperature, and the viscosity of gases increases with an increase in temperature. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: Thus, upon heating, liquids flow more easily, whereas gases flow more ____.
e: Thus, upon heating, liquids flow more easily, whereas gases flow more slowly. Heating raises gas viscosity, so gases flow more slowly.

q: Also, viscosity does not change as the amount of matter changes, therefore it is an ____ property.
e: Also, viscosity does not change as the amount of matter changes, therefore it is an intensive property. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: The SI unit of viscosity is ____ second (Pa s) which is equivalent to newton second per metre squared ($N s m^{-2}$).
e: The SI unit of viscosity is pascal second (Pa s) which is equivalent to newton second per metre squared (N s m⁻²). Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: One way is to measure fluid's resistance to flow when an external force is applied. This is known as ____ viscosity.
e: One way is to measure fluid's resistance to flow when an external force is applied. This is known as dynamic viscosity. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: And the other way is to measure the resistive flow of a fluid under the weight of gravity. It is known as ____ viscosity.
e: And the other way is to measure the resistive flow of a fluid under the weight of gravity. It is known as kinematic viscosity. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: Newton's law of viscosity states that the shear stress between the two adjacent layers of fluid is directly proportional to the ____ value of the velocity gradient between the same two adjacent fluid layers.
e: The blank is negative. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy). That word is the one that completes the idea about Newton law viscosity states shear stress.

q: Shear stress is the shearing force per unit ____.
e: Shear stress is the shearing force per unit area. area is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Viscosity is defined as the ratio of shearing stress to the ____ gradient.
e: Viscosity is defined as the ratio of shearing stress to the velocity gradient. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: Stokes' law expresses the ____ force resisting the fall of small spherical objects through a fluid medium under the influence of gravity.
e: Stokes' law expresses the drag force resisting the fall of small spherical objects through a fluid medium under the influence of gravity. Stokes' law gives the viscous drag on a small sphere as F = 6πηrv.

q: At a constant velocity of fall (terminal velocity), the upward and downward forces are in ____.
e: At a constant velocity of fall (terminal velocity), the upward and downward forces are in balance. balance is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Surface tension is the tendency of the surface of a liquid to behave like a stretched elastic ____ (or membrane).
e: Surface tension is the tendency of the surface of a liquid to behave like a stretched elastic skin (or membrane). Surface tension γ is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, γ = F/l.

q: Cohesion refers to forces between molecules of the ____ substance.
e: Cohesion refers to forces between molecules of the same substance. same is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: For example, cohesion makes water molecules pull together making the water surface to stretch like an elastic ____.
e: For example, cohesion makes water molecules pull together making the water surface to stretch like an elastic skin. skin is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Surface tension is the reason a water ____ and it is able to stride along water surface without sinking.
e: Surface tension is the reason a water strider and it is able to stride along water surface without sinking. Surface tension γ is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, γ = F/l.

q: Paperclips, razor blades and light coins are also able to rest on water without sinking although their density is ____ than that of water.
e: Paperclips, razor blades and light coins are also able to rest on water without sinking although their density is higher than that of water. The still fluid sits at higher pressure than the fast stream.

q: Surface tension is defined as the force per unit ____ that acts across any line on a surface tending to pull the surface apart.
e: Surface tension is defined as the force per unit length that acts across any line on a surface tending to pull the surface apart. Surface tension γ is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, γ = F/l.

q: The SI unit of surface tension is newton per ____ ($N m^{-1}$).
e: The SI unit of surface tension is newton per metre (N m⁻¹). Surface tension γ is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, γ = F/l.

q: Surface tension can also be referred to as a force because it is the tension between liquid ____.
e: Surface tension can also be referred to as a force because it is the tension between liquid molecules. Surface tension γ is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, γ = F/l.

q: Capillary action is defined as the spontaneous flow of a liquid into a narrow tube or ____ material.
e: Capillary action is defined as the spontaneous flow of a liquid into a narrow tube or porous material. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height.

q: Capillary action is caused by the combination of cohesive forces of the liquid and the ____ forces between the liquid and tube material.
e: Capillary action is caused by the combination of cohesive forces of the liquid and the adhesive forces between the liquid and tube material. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height.

q: Cohesion refers to forces between molecules of same substance; whereas, adhesion refers to forces between molecules of ____ substances.
e: Cohesion refers to forces between molecules of same substance; whereas, adhesion refers to forces between molecules of different substances. different is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: In order for wicking to occur, a tube needs to be sufficiently ____ in diameter.
e: In order for wicking to occur, a tube needs to be sufficiently small in diameter. small is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Capillary action is also the rise or depression of a liquid in a narrow tube of small cross-sectional area, like the spaces between the fibres of a towel or the openings in a ____ material.
e: Capillary action is also the rise or depression of a liquid in a narrow tube of small cross-sectional area, like the spaces between the fibres of a towel or the openings in a porous material. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height.

q: The rise of water underneath the ground is also the example of ____ action.
e: The rise of water underneath the ground is also the example of capillary action. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height.

q: Capillary action helps bringing water up into the ____.
e: Capillary action helps bringing water up into the roots. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height.

q: When a glass tube with a small inside diameter is dipped into water, the water rises into the tube; for example, a glass tube with a bore of about 1 mm in diameter, the water will rise to a height ____ cm.
e: The blank is 5. That word is the one that completes the idea about glass tube small inside diameter dipped.

q: The smaller the bore, the ____ the water will rise.
e: The smaller the bore, the higher the water will rise. The still fluid sits at higher pressure than the fast stream.

q: Liquids that rise in small bore tubes inserted into the liquid are said to ____ the tube, whereas liquids that are depressed within thin tubes below the surface of the surrounding liquid do not wet the tube.
e: The blank is wetting. That word is the one that completes the idea about Liquids rise small bore tubes inserted.

q: Water is a liquid that wets glass capillary tubes; ____ is one that does not.
e: Water is a liquid that wets glass capillary tubes; mercury is one that does not. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height.

q: Capillarity does not occur for non-____ liquids.
e: Capillarity does not occur for non-wetting liquids. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height.

q: When a glass tube is dipped into water, the ____ between glass and water causes a thin film of water to be drawn up over the inner and outer surfaces of the tube.
e: When a glass tube is dipped into water, the adhesion between glass and water causes a thin film of water to be drawn up over the inner and outer surfaces of the tube. adhesion is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Since the adhesive force is greater than cohesive force, water level rises until there is a sufficient mass of liquid for ____ forces to overcome these intermolecular forces.
e: Since the adhesive force is greater than cohesive force, water level rises until there is a sufficient mass of liquid for gravitational forces to overcome these intermolecular forces. gravitational is the word that belongs in that blank.
